newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- IMRO PROBES YOUNG TRUSTEES

Regulatory authorities investigating the Peter Young affair have turned their attention to the trustees of the Morgan Grenfell funds. The funds' accountant, KPMG, is not being investigated, as Imro, the Investment Management Regulatory Organization, does not regulate them.
-- BETTING IS ON FIVE POUNDS FOR A&L SHARES

Shares in Alliance & Leicester could reach five stg when trading starts on Monday. This price would mean A&L have a market capitalisation of 2.9 billion stg, compared with expectations of 2.5 billion stg. The first auction to institutions of shares being sold by members takes place today.
-- FEARS OF 2,000 JOB CUTS AS C&W CLEARS CABLE MERGER

Job cuts of up to 2,000 are likely, following the announcement by Cable & Wireless of the creation of C&W Communications, a 5 billion stg cable television and communications company in Britain. Shareholders unanimously approved the formation of the company through a merger of Mercury Communications, Nynex, Bell Cablemedia and Videotron.
THE TIMES
-- CO-OP SUSPENDS TWO AFTER LEAKS

The Co-operative Wholesale Society has suspended two senior staff, who are suspected of breach of trust relating to leaks of the annual report to the public relations firm acting for Andrew Regan of Lancia Trust. Regan is trying to buy parts of CWS.
Retail chief Allan Green and Co-operative Retail Trading Group head David Chambers were relieved of their duties yesterday morning.
-- INFLATION FALLS TO LOWEST FOR TWO YEARS

Underlying inflation dropped to 2.7 percent in March, the lowest level for two years, but still just short of the Government's inflation target of 2.5 percent by the election. Headline inflation also declined to 2.6 percent, down from 2.7 percent in February, according to the Office of National Statistics data.
-- TREASURY URGED TO REPAY PENSION FUND MILLIONS

The Treasury is under pressure to repay millions of pounds of surpluses, removed from occupational pension schemes when the associated companies were privatised. The Pensions Ombudsman has found in a number of separate rulings that surpluses should be removed, leading to a greatly increased caseload as more complaints follow.
THE GUARDIAN
-- HOUSE OF FRASER LOSES IN 'CRAP' GAME

House of Fraser said yesterday it had millions of pounds worth of 'crap' stock on its shelves, and that there was more to come, as the company is contracted to take delivery of goods. The company said it charged 53.2 million stg in exceptional costs for rationalisation. Pretax profit before exceptionals was 14.8 million stg, against 14.3 million stg last time.
-- EC FORCES ANGLO TO CUT STAKE IN LONRHO

Anglo American has offered to reduce its stake in Lonrho to below 10 percent after pressure from the European Commission, according to EU sources. The company holds a 28.4 percent stake at present. The commission believes the stake affects competition on the platinum market.
-- WORLD DEBT RESCUE IN JEOPARDY

Labour last night welcomed a report from Oxfam and pledged to help the world's poorest countries reduce their debt burden. The charity warned that a World Bank plan to reduce debt repayments was in jeopardy, after resistance to a rapid introduction from many countries, including the USA and Germany.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BT SPANISH COUP RED RAG TO AT&T BULL

British Telecom and MCI are today expected to sign a global alliance with Telefonica of Spain, in a huge coup over AT&T. The alliance will give Concert, the new BT/MCI global communications venture, a significant start in the rapidly expanding Latin American market.
-- NAMES WILL DIG DEEPER TO BACK UNDERWRITING

Lloyd's Names will be asked for extra funds to back their underwriting capacity if proposals unveiled yesterday are accepted. The changes are expected to move the market away from traditional backing by individuals with unlimited liability towards a market in the hands of limited-liability corporate members.
-- BAe RETURNS ON JET PASS LAUNCH AID INVESTMENT

British Aerospace revealed yesterday that repayments of launch aid for the Airbus A320 jet programme now exceed the 250 million stg received from the government in 1984. By the end of the decade, total payments would have reached 500 million stg, after which the government will receive a royalty on every A320 delivered. The company is seeking launch aid for the next Airbus project, the A3XX.
